title: podman machine (libkrun, macOS): `--volume ...:ro` is silently ignored - share is writable from the VM
body:
### Issue Description

On macOS with the default `libkrun` provider, VM volumes created with `:ro` are recorded as read-only in the machine config but are mounted and writable in the VM. Writes reach the host.

This gives a false sense of security - users expect `:ro` to protect host files from a compromised VM or container.

Temporary workaround suggestion:
If easy to implement, the guest mount config should state `ro`, as a defense-in-depth fallback.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Run:
```sh
mkdir ~/ro-test
podman machine init -v "$HOME/ro-test:$HOME/ro-test:ro"
podman machine start
podman machine ssh "echo hello > $HOME/ro-test/x"
cat ~/ro-test/x
```

### Describe the results you received

- `cat ~/ro-test/x` is successful, because the write from inside the VM was successful, although it should not have been.
- Machine config records the intent `"ReadOnly": true` for the mount in `~/.config/containers/podman/machine/libkrun/podman-machine-default.json`
- Guest mounts it read-write: `findmnt -t virtiofs -o TARGET,OPTIONS` → `rw,relatime,...`

### Describe the results you expected

The write fails (`Read-only file system`), ideally enforced on the host side, so guest root can't bypass it.
